His memorandum answered six questions from the Secretary of Defense's office covering the abruptness of the resignation, the 'uncertain provenance' of the second resignation letter, Elizondo's claim of secretly working for the Secretary, video handling, and the TTSA press conference.

label: Garry P. Reid
narrative: Reid is the author of the Department's internal counter-narrative. As Director for Defense Intelligence within OUSD(I) — the office running counterintelligence, security and law enforcement policy for the whole Department — he wrote the memoranda that first framed Elizondo as a man who 'aggrandized his role,' and those memoranda went to the Secretary of Defense. FOIA case 18-F-0324 released two of them: an undated memorandum for record on media reporting related to AATIP and Elizondo's actions, and a response to six questions put by the Secretary's office in late December 2017 concerning why Elizondo resigned, the 'uncertain provenance' of the second resignation letter, and the handling of the videos. Reid asserted that 'to the best of his knowledge' Elizondo 'had no job responsibilities related to the AATIP' — a formulation that became the Department's public line eighteen months later and has never been retracted. Reid is also the official Elizondo named in his May 2021 DoD Inspector General complaint. Reid was removed from his position by April 2022 after DoD IG investigations substantiated Joint Ethics Regulation violations, mishandling of controlled unclassified information via personal email on 65 occasions, and unwelcome physical contact with female subordinates. Defense officials told The Debrief that Reid 'played a central role in obfuscating information' about UAP.

The memo does not explain why an officer with no program responsibilities was the one processing the program's imagery five years after the program allegedly ended.
unverified: Whether Reid personally directed the June 2019 public statements; the released May 2019 messaging emails show Neill Tipton originating the 'no assigned responsibilities' formulation, with Reid's role described by unnamed defense officials rather than documents.
